Commentary.Commentary: Back with the chase! The players of the Bangladesh Women have walked out and are taking their respective positions. Also, the two openers of the Sri Lanka Women stride out where Chamari Athapaththu will open the innings alongside Hasini Perera. Marufa Akter has the new ball in her hands, and she will start the proceedings. Here we go...
... The Run Chase ...

Sri Lanka Women's bowlers played a significant role in restricting Bangladesh's scoring rate. Kavisha Dilhari and Dewmi Vihanga stood out, claiming 2 wickets each and proving to be the most effective bowlers for Sri Lanka. They will be banking on their batters to chase this down. Can they do it? We shall find out in the second innings.

Sharmin Akhter continued to anchor the innings with a fifty, but the team's inability to form meaningful partnerships at the non-striker's end hindered their progress. Despite Akhter's efforts, wickets continued to fall at regular intervals. She eventually fell in the 35th over after scoring 71 runs. The latter stages of the innings saw Sumaiya Akter and Fahima Khatun join forces, adding a valuable 58-run partnership to propel Bangladesh to this competitive total. Otherwise, things could have been different for them.

Bangladesh Women end their innings at a fightable total of 242/8. They got off to a cautious start, losing Farzana Haque early in the innings. However, Rubya Haider and Sharmin Akhter steadied the ship with a steady partnership, adding 90 runs together. Although the partnership was built at a slow pace, it provided a crucial foundation for Bangladesh's innings. Rubya Haider's departure in the 19th over briefly disrupted the momentum.
